slides.title: Trees and Traversals
slides.main: File systems, markup, expressions: all of them are trees.

captions: File system, page markup, expressions: data branches
The root has children, and they have their own
This is how a tree grows: every node is the root of its subtree
Traversal trees, search trees, heaps, red-black trees

body.text: Fourteen exercises: from iterative traversals to the prefix tree.

slides.title: Terms
slides.main: The key number of a tree is its height: operation cost depends on it.

captions: The root is the top node; all others have exactly one parent
Nodes without children are leaves (green)
Any node with all its descendants is a subtree
Tree height is the greatest depth: the key number for operation cost

slides.title: How to store a tree
slides.main: A complete tree fits in an array: children of node i are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2.

captions: Each node has a value and links to its children
A complete tree needs just an array: root at 0, level after level
Children of node i are at 2i + 1 and 2i + 2: arithmetic instead of links

slides.title: Recursive pattern
slides.sub: Base case and combining children's answers
slides.main: Empty tree is the base; a node's answer is built from its subtrees' answers.

captions: Base: an empty tree has height 0
Leaf: 1 + max(0, 0) = 1
Node: 1 + max(children's heights): B = 1 + max(1, 1) = 2
Root: 1 + max(2, 2) = 3, in one bottom-up traversal

slides.title: Depth-first traversals
slides.main: The three orders differ in when the node is visited.

captions: Preorder: node, left, right; parent before children (copying, saving)
Inorder: left, node, right; on a search tree gives ascending values
Postorder: left, right, node; children before parent (deleting, evaluating)
The visit moment of the node is the only difference between the three

slides.title: Explicit stack
slides.main: A degenerate tree overflows the call stack: keep your own stack.

captions: Going left, pushing nodes onto the stack: 4, 2, 1
Nothing on the left: pop 1, process it; nothing on the right: pop the next
Pop 2, process it; go to the right subtree: push 3
No recursion depth needed: an explicit stack handles a chain of 100,000 nodes

slides.title: Breadth-first traversal
slides.main: Batches of the level size from a queue give separate levels.

captions: Queue with the root: process it, put its children at the tail
Second level: 2 and 6 (left to right)
Third level: 1, 3, 5, 7
Batches of the queue size give separate levels; memory is the tree width

slides.title: Tree diameter
slides.main: The function returns the height and updates the best path through the node.

captions: The function returns the subtree height (in edges)
Through A: left 2 + right 2 = 4, path D-B-A-C-G
Through R: 3 + 0 = 3, which is less
Diameter = 4; the path avoids the root. One traversal, linear time

slides.title: Lowest common ancestor
slides.main: Both subtrees returned an answer: the current node is the ancestor.

captions: We need the lowest common ancestor of nodes 6 and 2
The left subtree of node 5 returned 6: target found
The right subtree returned 2
Both answers are non-empty: node 5 is the ancestor; the root gets an answer only from the left

slides.title: Rebuilding from traversals
slides.main: The root is first in preorder; inorder shows the subtree sizes.

captions: Preorder and inorder sequences (values are distinct)
The first preorder element is the root; find it in the inorder
Left of the root is the left subtree (1 node), right is the right one (3 nodes); and so on
Tree rebuilt: this is what serialization relies on

slides.title: Not only binary
slides.main: Nested structures are trees; traverse them with recursion.

captions: A directory has any number of subdirectories: a tree with any number of children
Page elements are nested in each other: the same traversal
Dictionaries in dictionaries and lists in lists form a tree; recursion with a type check

slides.title: Prefix tree
slides.sub: A path from the root reads a string
slides.main: Word and prefix lookup costs the word length, not the dictionary size.

captions: Each edge is a character; a path from the root reads a string
Inserted cat: path c → a → t
car shares the prefix "ca" with cat: only the new node r was added
dog is a separate branch; all operations cost the word length, not the word count
All words starting with "ca" are the subtree of node a: cat and car

slides.title: Height decides
slides.sub: A bushy tree versus a chain
slides.main: A balanced tree has height log n; a chain has n.

captions: 7 nodes, height 3: search takes three steps
The same 7 nodes as a chain: height 7, like a linked list
In a database index a node holds hundreds of keys: 3–4 hops for billions of records

slides.title: Summary and practice
slides.sub: What we carry into the next chapters
slides.main: Terms, recursive pattern, traversals, techniques: the basis of search trees.

captions: Root, children, leaves; the key number is the height
Empty tree is the base; a node's answer comes from its children's
Depth-first: stack or recursion; breadth-first: queue
Return one thing, accumulate another; lowest common ancestor
Iterative traversals, levels, symmetry, rebuilding, prefix tree
